note: Moderate-to-severe Crohn's: tofacitinib failed two phase 2 programs (2014, 2017) with no published colitis-model data behind them, filgotinib was positive in FITZROY (2017) then mixed in DIVERSITY (2025), upadacitinib was approved in 2023; no colitis model was relied on to take any of them into Crohn's, and none has been shown to separate Crohn's from UC.
label: Crohn's (JAK)

engagement.note: Tofacitinib gave maximal inhibition of colonic STAT1 phosphorylation in mice; no Crohn's-patient pSTAT comparison has been published.
engagement.quote: Tofacitinib, dosed orally, intracecally, or applied to the colonic lumen in vitro, produced dose-dependent, and maximal inhibition of oxazolone or IFNγ-induced STAT1 phosphorylation in the colon.
engagement.reason: No mouse–patient pSTAT comparison in Crohn's
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level reading (open access, PMC5718031). Patient-side engagement signal exists without a model counterpart: in the phase 2b induction trial CRP fell significantly on tofacitinib while clinical remission did not separate from placebo (Panés 2017, doi:10.1136/gutjnl-2016-312735). No paper puts a mouse pSTAT/cytokine readout beside a Crohn's-patient readout, so untested.

efficacy.note: First published colitis-model use of a class member: tofacitinib improved oxazolone colitis. Tofacitinib's Crohn's phase 2 trials (2008–2015) had already run.
efficacy.quote: Tofacitinib, dosed orally or intracecally, inhibited, with similar efficacy, oxazolone-induced colitis, represented by improvements in the disease activity index and its sub-scores (body weight, stool consistency and blood content).
efficacy.judgement: Abstract-level reading. PubMed search for any JAK inhibitor (tofacitinib/CP-690,550, filgotinib/GLPG0634, upadacitinib/ABT-494, 'JAK inhibitor') in a mouse or rat colitis model up to 2017 returned this paper only; the filgotinib (Van Rompaey 2013, doi:10.4049/jimmunol.1201348) and upadacitinib (Parmentier 2018, doi:10.1186/s41927-018-0031-x) preclinical characterisations used arthritis models, not colitis. The class entered Crohn's trials on RA/UC data, not on a colitis model.

efficacy.note: Therapeutic tofacitinib ameliorated T-cell transfer colitis, yet the same paper notes tofacitinib works in UC patients but not Crohn's.
efficacy.short: Mouse responded; Crohn's patients did not
efficacy.quote: Moreover tofacitinib is efficacious in patients with active UC but not Crohn’s disease (CD), which can be explained that JAK/STAT molecules play pleiotropic and cell specific roles.
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call. Full text read (PMC9992375). The paper's own result is 'Tofacitinib is effective in the treatment of murine experimental T cell transfer colitis, however does not prevent occurrence of disease', and its discussion sets that beside the clinical UC-yes/Crohn's-no outcome in one sentence; it does not itself label the T-cell transfer model Crohn's-like or call the result a miss, so comparison_stated=true is generous and a reviewer could downgrade this to untested. Patient side: Sandborn 2014 (doi:10.1016/j.cgh.2014.01.029; NCT00615199, results posted 2012-12-31) and Panés 2017 (doi:10.1136/gutjnl-2016-312735; NCT01393626 results posted 2017-04-28, NCT01393899 posted 2017-01-09), both placebo-level clinical remission. The models also disagree with each other: Liu 2026 (doi:10.1038/s41467-026-71808-y, full text read) found tofacitinib non-protective in wild-type DSS and T-cell transfer colitis while upadacitinib and filgotinib protected, a pattern that matches the Crohn's clinic (upadacitinib approved: Loftus 2023, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2212728, NCT03345849 results posted 2022-11-23) but the paper compares only with UC patients and never mentions Crohn's, so it cannot change the status here. No published JAK-inhibitor study in SAMP1/YitFc ileitis or TNBS colitis was found that compares with Crohn's patients.
